Principal Problem: Adjustment to acute vertigo episode
- Patient Goal(s): Regain physical stability, reduce dizziness-related discomfort, maintain daily functioning
- Clinical Goal(s): Resolve vertigo, monitor for secondary anxiety, ensure adequate support
- Actions (Patient): • Take prescribed vestibular-suppressant as directed • Arrange in-person GP assessment • Seek urgent care if neurological “red flags” (weakness, new headache, vomiting) occur
- Actions (Clinician/GP): • Provide prescription to local pharmacy • Arrange face-to-face examination (ear inspection, BP, neuro exam) • Educate patient on red-flag symptoms • Reassess mental wellbeing if vertigo persists

- Coping Strategies: Rest, positional caution when dizzy, seek support from husband, scheduled follow-up

- Vestibular neuritis / viral labyrinthitis – High likelihood: Continuous spinning vertigo, tinnitus, gait unsteadiness without focal deficits
- Ménière’s disease – Medium likelihood: Recurrent vertigo with tinnitus; hearing loss absent
- Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) – Medium-Low likelihood: Prior brief episode could fit, but current continuous vertigo not typical
